qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number'; runtime evidence section)
evidence:
NESTING (static arithmetic, verified): task.toml differs from the frozen template only in [task]/[metadata] text; timeouts are template-canonical: [agent] timeout_sec=7200.0, [environment] build_timeout_sec=600.0, [verifier] timeout_sec=13200.0. test.sh (byte-identical to template) runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (test.sh:207), so judges in a suite run sequentially: gates budget `run_suite gates 1500` (test.sh:213) vs render 600 + constraints 600 = 1200 < 1500 (each 600 < 1500). Scored budget `run_suite scored 11100` (test.sh:224) vs functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 < 11100. 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 verifier. Liveness: probe loop 120 x 0.25 s (test.sh:116-121) ~30 s plus up to 2 s urlopen per URL, and it runs before the suites (worst case ~8 min only if both probes hang, and 12600 + startup still < 13200 by 600 s; realistic Node start is seconds). Restart helper waits 30 s for readiness (app-restart.sh, test.sh:171-182) inside restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 (restart_mcp.py:11). Agent image build is apt + two pinned global npm installs (environment/Dockerfile), plausibly far under 600 s. All nest correctly; check-scoring-policy's nesting rule is satisfied.

LONG ENOUGH (unmeasured): the workload is far heavier than the template's at the same canonical budget. Functional judge.toml has 43 binary criteria (template: 2) in one batched claude-code session with timeout 9000 (~209 s per criterion), driven by an 18,004-byte prompt containing 14 multi-actor protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D) with many independent browser contexts, captured/replayed requests, a restart, and repeated 'wait up to 15 seconds' live-update readings (U alone has roughly 8-10 such waits; V more). Polish (5 criteria, 900 s) also includes two 15 s live waits plus multi-context setup. raw-evidence-index.json scope states explicitly: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent', and each entry says 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' Scripted Playwright duration is not judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY). So there is no measured evidence that the GLM-5.3-flashx claude-code judge finishes Functional within 9000 s or Polish within 900 s. Per SKILL.md, an unmeasured claim cannot be upgraded to Pass; the nesting half passes, the 'long enough' half is Not exercised and remains a delivery risk. I do not recommend an automatic increase; current budgets are canonical and policy forbids changing them without a measured reason.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app that delivers live updates by polling every 10-12 s (allowed by the 15 s windows) forces the judge to sit out most of each 15 s window across the U/V/polish protocols, and a slower flash judge doing ~43 criteria with many fresh contexts could exceed functional timeout=9000 (or polish 900). A timed-out judge leaves functional at 0/unscored, failing the functional floor 0.05 (scoring.toml) or tripping `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0` (test.sh:224-225) to the zero reward, so a correct submission would score 0 for a harness reason. Not demonstrated; no full configured run exists to confirm or refute it.
suggested_fix: Run the full configured verifier (claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx) on the golden at least once, record per-dimension judge wall time in a hash-bound workload record; if Functional approaches 9000 s or Polish 900 s, reduce redundant browser work/scope, or make a recorded, authorized timeout change kept below five hours with the checker adapted narrowly.
